app.privacy.title: Privacy Policy
app.privacy.s1.title: 1. Data Controller
app.privacy.s1.body: The data controller is Javier Garcia Mateos (tax ID 07991565P), Avenida de los Tulipanes 30, 46185 La Pobla de Vallbona (Valencia), Spain, owner of Finanverso (finanverso.app). Contact: support@finanverso.app. The server is hosted by Hetzner Online GmbH (Helsinki, Finland), within the European Union, so processing is governed by the General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR).
app.privacy.s2.title: 2. Data We Collect
app.privacy.s2.intro: To provide the service we process this data:
app.privacy.s2.item1: Name and email address (registration and authentication).
app.privacy.s2.item2: Password (stored encrypted with bcrypt; never in plain text).
app.privacy.s2.item3: Optional profile picture (an image you upload yourself).
app.privacy.s2.item4: Personal financial data: transactions (amount, description, category, date), categories, budgets and automation rules you enter.
app.privacy.s2.item5: Session tokens and preferences stored on your device (see section 8).
app.privacy.s3.title: 3. Purpose and Legal Basis
app.privacy.s3.intro: We use your data for these purposes, each with its legal basis (art. 6 GDPR):
app.privacy.s3.item1: Providing the service and its features: accounts, transactions, budgets, goals, statement import, shared expenses and the private receipts address, whose e-mails we read to create the expense (performance of the contract, art. 6.1.b).
app.privacy.s3.item2: Sending you transactional e-mails: account verification, password recovery and purchase confirmation (performance of the contract).
app.privacy.s3.item3: AI (Premium): questions and analyses, only when you ask for them, and categorisation when importing statements, only if you turn on "Suggest categories with AI" in the import screen; it is off by default (consent, art. 6.1.a).
app.privacy.s3.noMarketing: We do no marketing, we do not sell your data and we do not build profiles that affect you.
app.privacy.s4.title: 4. Providers and international transfers
app.privacy.s4.p1: We do not sell or share your data for commercial purposes. To provide the service we use these providers, which process the data on our behalf unless stated otherwise:
app.privacy.s4.item1: Hetzner Online GmbH (Germany; server in Helsinki, Finland): hosting of the application, the database and the backups.
app.privacy.s4.item2: Cloudflare, Inc. (USA): all finanverso.app traffic goes through Cloudflare, which acts as reverse proxy and terminates TLS encryption, so it sees your IP address and the requests in transit. It also receives the e-mails you forward to your facturas.finanverso.app address (Email Routing and a Worker) and delivers them to us.
app.privacy.s4.item3: AI provider (Premium), Cloudflare Workers AI or Google Gemini (paid API) depending on the service configuration. When you ask the AI or request an analysis we send your question, your category names and the aggregated figures of the period. If you turn on AI categorisation when importing, we send the transaction descriptions without long digit sequences (IBAN, cards); they may include names of shops or people. Under their terms, they do not use this data to train their models.
app.privacy.s5.title: 5. Data Retention
app.privacy.s5.p1: We keep each piece of data only as long as needed:
app.privacy.s5.item1: Your account and the data you enter: while you have the account. When you delete it, they are erased from the database at once.
app.privacy.s5.item2: Daily backups and copies taken before each database update: 14 days. After that, whatever you deleted is gone from them too.
app.privacy.s5.item3: Server technical logs: rotated automatically, at most 30 MB per service.
app.privacy.s5.item4: Clicks in "Offers", usage counters (AI, income tax) and the push notice log: while you have the account.
app.privacy.s5.item5: E-mails forwarded to your receipts address: we do not keep the e-mail, only the outcome of the last 50 (date, status, merchant and amount).
app.privacy.s5.item6: Acceptance of the terms and request for immediate start: while you have the account; erased when you delete it.
app.privacy.s5.item7: Stripe keeps the payments, invoices and your customer record for the period required by tax law, also after you delete your account.
app.privacy.s5.item8: RevenueCat and Google Play keep the record of your Android purchases (with your user id, without name or e-mail) to meet their billing obligations.
app.privacy.s6.title: 6. Security
app.privacy.s6.p1: We apply the following technical measures:
app.privacy.s6.item2: Passwords hashed with bcrypt (high cost factor).
app.privacy.s6.item3: Authentication via short-lived JWT tokens with refresh token.
app.privacy.s6.item4: Technical logs store no financial data and no IP addresses; they are rotated automatically, at most 30 MB per service.
app.privacy.s7.title: 7. Your Rights (GDPR)
app.privacy.s7.intro: As a user you have the right to:
app.privacy.s7.item1: Access: download a copy of all your data from "Settings → Your data" or ask us for it.
app.privacy.s7.item2: Rectification: correct inaccurate data from your profile.
app.privacy.s7.item3: Erasure ('right to be forgotten'): delete your account and all associated data.
app.privacy.s7.item4: Portability: export all your data as JSON, or your movements as CSV, from "Settings → Your data".
app.privacy.s7.item5: Objection, restriction and withdrawal of consent: turn the feature off or write to us.
app.privacy.s7.item6: Complaint: if you believe we have violated your rights you may lodge a complaint with the Spanish Data Protection Agency (aepd.es) or your local supervisory authority.
app.privacy.s7.how: To exercise any of these rights write to support@finanverso.app from your account's e-mail; we will reply within one month at most. You can also export your data and delete your account yourself in the app.
app.privacy.s8.title: 8. Cookies and Local Storage
app.privacy.s8.p1: We use no tracking cookies and no third-party analytics. The app stores in your browser or phone (localStorage) only what it needs to work, and does not send it to third parties:
app.privacy.s8.item1: Session: the access tokens and your name and e-mail.
app.privacy.s8.item2: Preferences: theme, language, "Remember me" on sign-in, the AI option for imports, the PIN lock, the last tab and notices already seen.
app.privacy.s8.item3: Income tax and self-employed drafts and the tax office checklist: they stay on your device.
app.privacy.s8.item4: Payments captured from notifications (Android), until you decide whether to add them.
app.privacy.s8.item5: Invitation codes (from a friend or a household) while you complete the sign-up.
app.privacy.s8.item6: Sign-up source: the site or campaign you came from, kept in your browser until you sign in; then it is added to an anonymous counter, not linked to your account, and erased.
app.privacy.s8.p2: To know whether the service works we keep aggregated, anonymous counters on our server (for example, how many signups or purchases there were each day). They contain no personal data, are not linked to any account and we use no third-party analytics tools.
app.privacy.s8.p3: When you sign out or delete the account we erase all of this from the device, except the theme, the language and, when signing out, the e-mail if you ticked "Remember me".
app.privacy.s9.title: 9. Minors
app.privacy.s9.p1: The service is meant for people aged 14 or over, the age from which Spanish law (art. 7 LOPDGDD) allows consenting to the processing of one's own data. If you are under 14 you must not create an account or give us personal data. By signing up you confirm you are 14 or older.
app.privacy.s10.title: 10. Changes to This Policy
app.privacy.s10.p1: We may update this policy occasionally. We will notify you via an in-app notice. The last updated date will always be visible at the top of this page.
app.privacy.s11.title: 11. Account Deletion
app.privacy.s11.p1: You can permanently delete your account and all associated data directly from within the app at any time. No email or external form is required.
app.privacy.s11.step1: Open the app and log in.
app.privacy.s11.step2: Tap the profile icon (top right) to open your profile.
app.privacy.s11.step3: Scroll down and open the "Settings" section.
app.privacy.s11.step4: Tap "Delete account" and confirm in the dialog.
app.privacy.s11.p2: On confirmation we erase at once your profile and photo, accounts, transactions, categories and rules, budgets, goals, automations, alerts, investments and debts, shared expenses, your receipts address and its history, invitations, push subscriptions, subscription data, terms acceptance and usage counters. They disappear from the backups within 14 days at most. Stripe keeps your payments and invoices, and RevenueCat the record of your Android purchases, for tax and billing obligations. If you own a shared household, the other person loses access to that data, including what they added; if you are a member, what you added stays in the owner's account.

terms.s2.title: 2. Plans
terms.s2.body: To use Finanverso you must be 14 or older; to buy a paid plan you must be of legal age or have your parents' or guardians' permission. The Free plan costs nothing and includes, with usage limits: 3 accounts, 5 budgets, 2 savings goals, 5 recurring movements, 3 custom alerts, 3 investments, assets or debts in total, 1 bank statement import, the forecast for next month, a summary of the detected subscriptions (the total and the 3 most expensive), 1 self-employed tax draft per quarter (of the current quarter or of the one being filed) and the download of one of them as a PDF, 3 tax return calculations per campaign, 1 AI analysis per month and chapters 1 and 2 of the "Learn to invest" course. Premium removes those limits and also includes the forecast of up to 12 months, trends by category, net worth evolution and the annual report, the whole course and the Premium videos of the Video library, receipts by e-mail, payments detected in bank notifications (Android), the shared household and the AI advisor with free questions (with a monthly maximum of analyses). Prices are shown in euros, VAT included. In addition, the tax return draft reader (which reads your draft and suggests deductions) is not part of the free trial: it is included after more than 2 months of paid Premium or with the tax return pass.
terms.s3.title: 3. Free trial
terms.s3.body: New accounts get 14 days of Premium at no cost and without a card. Afterwards the account moves to the Free plan and keeps all its data.
terms.s4.title: 4. Payment, renewal and cancellation
terms.s4.body: Payments are processed by Stripe; we never receive your card details. Before paying you must accept these terms; we keep the date and the version you accepted. Premium costs 3.49 € per month, 29.99 € per year or 59 € in a single payment with the Founder plan (limited to 100 places), VAT included. Monthly and yearly subscriptions renew automatically at the end of each period until you cancel them in "Your plan → Manage subscription". After cancelling you are not charged again and you keep Premium until the end of the period already paid; the unused part of the period is not refunded. The Founder plan is a one-time payment that grants Premium for as long as the service is available. The tax return pass is a one-time payment of 10 € (VAT included) that gives 30 days of use of the draft reader and of the tax return calculator without limit; it is not a subscription and does not renew. If you buy it in the Android app, Google Play processes the payment.
terms.s5.title: 5. Right of withdrawal
terms.s5.body: Premium starts as soon as you pay. That is why, when you buy, we ask you to expressly request that immediate start and to acknowledge that you therefore lose the 14-day right of withdrawal; we confirm it by e-mail together with the purchase. Before paying you get a 14-day free Premium trial to decide. All of this without prejudice to the rights the law grants you as a consumer. The same applies to the tax return pass: it is activated as soon as you pay.
terms.s6.title: 6. AI and partner offers
terms.s6.body: AI-generated analyses are for guidance only and are not financial advice. The "Offers" section contains sponsored links labelled as such, which you can hide in Settings. The tax return calculator and the draft reader are for guidance only: they do not replace the Tax Agency or a tax adviser, and the return is always your responsibility. app.tour.welcome.title: 👋 Welcome to Finanverso!

app.tour.budgets.title: 🎯 Budgets

tools.salary.faq1.q: How much Social Security comes off a Spanish payslip in 2026?
tools.salary.faq1.a: With a permanent contract, 6.50 % of your contribution base: 4.70 % common contingencies, 1.55 % unemployment, 0.10 % vocational training and 0.15 % MEI. With a temporary contract, unemployment goes up to 1.60 %. The base is capped at €5,101.20 a month; pay above that also bears the solidarity contribution.
tools.salary.faq2.q: Why do I get less per month with 14 payments?
tools.salary.faq2.a: Because the same yearly salary is split into 14 payments instead of 12. Social Security comes off the 12 monthly payments, since the extra ones are already spread over the base, so only income tax is withheld from the extra payments.
tools.salary.faq3.q: Does my region change the withholding on my payslip?
tools.salary.faq3.a: No. Employers work out the withholding with a single scale for all of Spain, except in the Basque Country and Navarre, which have their own. The region does count in the tax return: that is why the calculator estimates separately whether you would pay or get money back.
tools.salary.faq4.q: I earn the minimum wage: is income tax withheld?
tools.salary.faq4.a: It can be. With €17,094 a year, the 2026 minimum wage, a person without children is above the €15,876 limit under which nothing is withheld, although the withholding is capped at 43 % of the difference. tools.reta.faq1.q: How is the self-employed fee worked out in 2026?
tools.reta.faq1.a: It starts from the net income of your business (income minus deductible expenses, without taking off the fee itself), takes off 7 % for general expenses, or 3 % for company partners, and divides it by 12. That monthly income sets your bracket, and within it you choose a base between the minimum and the maximum. The fee is 31.5 % of the base.
tools.reta.faq2.q: How much is the autónomo flat rate in 2026?
tools.reta.faq2.a: The reduced fee for people registering for the first time, or after two years without being self-employed (three if they had it before), is €80 a month for 12 months, and it can be extended 12 more if your yearly net income is below the minimum wage (€17,094 in 2026). The law leaves the 2026 amount to the State Budget, which has not been passed, so we use the latest official figure.
tools.reta.faq3.q: What if I end up earning more or less than expected?
tools.reta.faq3.a: The following year Social Security compares your base with the income the Tax Agency reports and adjusts: it refunds what you paid in excess or claims the difference. You can change your base up to six times a year to match what you are earning.
tools.reta.faq4.q: What is the 7 % for general expenses?
tools.reta.faq4.a: A fixed deduction Social Security applies to your net income without you having to justify it. It is 3 % for directors with 25 % or more of the company and partners with 33 % or more, if they have been registered at least 90 days in the year. It is not the same as the income tax deduction for hard-to-justify expenses.

tools.invest.guide.title: How to declare this, step by step
tools.invest.guide.intro: What to do in Renta WEB with what you imported. It is a guide: if in doubt, ask a registered tax adviser. The app files nothing with the Tax Agency.
tools.invest.guide.unconfirmed: This step has something NOT CONFIRMED in an official source: check it with more care.
tools.invest.guide.before.title: 1. Have your papers at hand
tools.invest.guide.before.body: You need your access to Renta WEB (Cl@ve, certificate or reference number) and the report of this screen (download it as Excel or PDF).
tools.invest.guide.draft.title: 2. Open your draft and look at the tax data
tools.invest.guide.draft.body: In Renta WEB, your draft already brings what banks and some platforms reported (for example, sales of Spanish funds, interest, dividends and «reported virtual currencies» notices). Compare that data with the table of this screen. If it does not match, correct it in Renta WEB with your figures and keep the proof.
tools.invest.guide.funds.title: 3. Investment funds and ETFs
tools.invest.guide.funds.body: Go to «Ganancias y pérdidas patrimoniales» → «Transmisiones de acciones o participaciones de instituciones de inversión colectiva». Press «Alta» once per fund: type the fund's tax ID (it is on your bank's certificate), the transmission value (box 0312) and the acquisition value (box 0315) of the table. With a Spanish bank it usually comes filled in: just check it.
tools.invest.guide.onlySwitches.title: Transfers between funds: nothing to declare
tools.invest.guide.onlySwitches.body: If you only moved money from one fund to another by a transfer (without taking it out), you pay no tax now: the new fund keeps the cost and dates of the old one (art. 94 of the Personal Income Tax Act). Write nothing for the transfers. ETFs cannot be transferred like that.
tools.invest.guide.shares.title: 4. Shares
tools.invest.guide.shares.body: Go to «Ganancias y pérdidas patrimoniales derivadas de transmisiones de acciones negociadas». Press «Alta» once per company: type its name, the amount of the sales (box 0328) and the acquisition value (box 0331). If a loss does not count this year because you bought again within two months, the table says so.
tools.invest.guide.crypto.title: 5. Crypto
tools.invest.guide.crypto.body: Go to «Ganancias y pérdidas patrimoniales derivadas de la transmisión o permuta de monedas virtuales». Press «Alta» per coin and kind of consideration: type the name (for example, «bitcoin»), choose in the drop-down what you received in exchange (in the table: key F if it was money, key N if it was another virtual currency; these letters are NOT CONFIRMED in an official source, look at the drop-down) and copy the transmission value (box 1804) and the acquisition value (box 1806). The Tax Agency works out each sale separately: if Renta WEB asks for one line per sale, use the «Ventas y FIFO» sheet of the report. We found no official way to import a file of gains into Renta WEB: it has to be typed (NOT CONFIRMED).
tools.invest.guide.other.title: 6. Derivatives, CFDs, gold and others
tools.invest.guide.other.body: We put the results of derivatives and leveraged positions in «Ganancias y pérdidas derivadas de transmisiones de otros elementos patrimoniales» (boxes 1624 to 1640), one per position or grouped by year of closing. It is a NOT CONFIRMED criterion: some advisers put them in «other gains». Ask an adviser if you have many positions.
tools.invest.guide.capital.title: 7. Interest, dividends and staking
tools.invest.guide.capital.body: Go to «Rendimientos del capital mobiliario». Interest and staking or lending rewards: box 0027 ({interest} €). Dividends: box 0029 ({dividends} €). Bills and bonds: box 0031 ({assets} €). Type the Spanish withholdings in box 0597 and the custody fees in 0037. That staking goes in 0027 is NOT CONFIRMED: the Directorate General of Taxes says it is capital income, but not which box.
tools.invest.guide.general.title: 8. Airdrops and other rewards
tools.invest.guide.general.body: Airdrops, crypto cashback and referral or learn rewards are added as «Otras ganancias imputables» (box 0304), in the general base. It is a NOT CONFIRMED criterion for each case: check it.
tools.invest.guide.foreign.title: 9. Tax paid abroad
tools.invest.guide.foreign.body: If tax was withheld abroad (for example, on US dividends), go to «Deducción por doble imposición internacional» (box 0588) and type the income obtained abroad and the tax paid. It only goes down to what the treaty with that country allows (often 15 %). What was withheld in excess is claimed in that country.
tools.invest.guide.losses.title: 10. Losses of this year and of earlier years
tools.invest.guide.losses.body: Renta WEB offsets the gains and losses of this year by itself. If you have losses of the 4 earlier years, check in the draft, in «Compensación de saldos negativos de ejercicios anteriores», that they are there; if not, type them. Only those declared in their year count. What cannot be offset is kept for the next 4 years.
tools.invest.guide.earlier.title: Sales of earlier years
tools.invest.guide.earlier.body: Your files have sales or income of past years. Each one is declared in the return of its year. If you did not, file a corrective return for that year (see «How to correct»). The Tax Agency can review the last 4 years.
tools.invest.guide.m721.title: Form 721: crypto abroad
tools.invest.guide.m721.body: If on 31 December you had crypto held by foreign companies (Binance, Coinbase, Kraken…) worth over 50,000 € in total, you have to file form 721 between 1 January and 31 March of the next year, on the Tax Agency's website. It is informative: nothing is paid. Coins you hold yourself (Ledger, MetaMask) do not go in form 721. According to your files it could be about {amount} €: check it with the real value on 31 December.
tools.invest.guide.m720.title: Form 720: securities and accounts abroad
tools.invest.guide.m720.body: If on 31 December you had shares, funds or accounts with foreign entities (Degiro, Interactive Brokers, eToro…) worth over 50,000 € in one group, you have to file form 720 between 1 January and 31 March of the next year. It is informative. According to your files it could be about {amount} €.
tools.invest.guide.activity.title: If you do it as a business
tools.invest.guide.activity.body: Organised mining, or trading with the means of a business, is declared as an economic activity, not as savings. Use the self-employed section of the app.
tools.invest.guide.deadline.title: Deadlines
tools.invest.guide.deadline.body: The return is filed in spring of the next year (the 2025 one, from 8 April to 30 June 2026). If you pay by direct debit, the last day is before the end.
tools.invest.guide.rectify.title: How to correct a return already filed
tools.invest.guide.rectify.body: If you forgot sales or typed a wrong figure, file a corrective return (autoliquidación rectificativa): in Renta WEB, open that year's return and choose the option to correct it (it works to pay more or to ask for a refund). If you have to pay, the sooner you file it the smaller the surcharge.
tools.invest.guide.keep.title: What to keep and for how long
tools.invest.guide.keep.body: Keep the reports of each platform, the statements with purchase and sale dates, the exchange rates used and this report, at least 4 years from the end of the filing period of the return where you declared the sale. If you sell something bought many years ago, also keep the proof of purchase.
tools.invest.guide.gestor.title: Check it with a professional if in doubt
tools.invest.guide.gestor.body: This is a guide, not tax advice. With many operations, DeFi, derivatives or large amounts, ask a registered tax adviser before filing.

app.autonomo.hint: From your professional income and expenses we prepare the draft of modelo 303 (VAT) and modelo 130 (income tax advance), with the boxes of the form, your estimated contribution and the deadlines.

hacienda.start.title: Before you start: how to identify yourself to the tax office
hacienda.start.description: Cl@ve, Cl@ve Móvil, digital certificate, electronic ID card, the Renta reference number and powers of attorney, made easy.
hacienda.start.intro: To do almost anything on the Agencia Tributaria website (the «sede electrónica») you have to prove it is you. The main ways are Cl@ve, a digital certificate and the electronic ID card (DNIe); for the Renta a reference number also works. Pick one and set it up in good time, not on the last day.
hacienda.start.which.title: Choose how you will identify yourself
hacienda.start.which.p1: Cl@ve is the easiest for most people: you register once and then sign in with the Cl@ve app on your phone, with no passwords to remember.
hacienda.start.which.p2: A digital certificate is a file you install on your computer or phone. It takes a bit more effort to get, but it works for almost everything and many self-employed people use it.
hacienda.start.which.p3: The electronic ID card also works if you have a card reader (or a compatible phone) and know your ID card PIN.
hacienda.start.which.p4: For the Renta there is also the reference number: a code you request with your ID and a figure from last year’s return. It only works for the Renta services, not for forms 303 or 130.
hacienda.start.which.c1: I have decided which method I will use.
hacienda.start.which.tip: If you are self-employed, keep two methods ready (for example Cl@ve and a certificate): if one fails on the last day, you still have the other.
hacienda.start.clave.title: Register for Cl@ve (only once)
hacienda.start.clave.p1: On the Agencia Tributaria website, in the Cl@ve section, look for «Registrarse en Cl@ve» (register for Cl@ve). There are several ways:
hacienda.start.clave.p2: Video identification from the Cl@ve app: download the official app on your phone, take a photo of your DNI or NIE and a short video of your face. It is the fastest way.
hacienda.start.clave.p3: Online with an invitation letter: you request it on the website and a letter with a code to finish the registration arrives by post.
hacienda.start.clave.p4: With your digital certificate or electronic ID card if you already have one, or in person at a registration office (for example of the Agencia Tributaria), with an appointment.
hacienda.start.clave.p5: Depending on how you register you get a basic or an advanced level. Basic (automatic video identification or invitation letter) works for many procedures, but not all. Advanced (with a certificate or electronic ID, in person, or with the video identification reviewed by a civil servant) works for more services.
hacienda.start.clave.c1: I have installed the official Cl@ve app on my phone.
hacienda.start.clave.c2: I have finished registering for Cl@ve.
hacienda.start.clave.c3: I have tried signing in to the tax website with Cl@ve.
hacienda.start.clave.warn: Cl@ve is personal: never share your access, not even with an accountant. If someone has to do things for you, use a power of attorney (last step of this guide).
hacienda.start.login.title: How to sign in with Cl@ve Móvil
hacienda.start.login.p1: In the procedure you want to do, choose to identify yourself with Cl@ve Móvil.
hacienda.start.login.p2: Open the Cl@ve app and scan the QR code on the screen. If you cannot scan it, you will get a notification on your phone to confirm it is you.
hacienda.start.login.c1: I know how to sign in with Cl@ve Móvil.
hacienda.start.cert.title: If you prefer a digital certificate
hacienda.start.cert.p1: The personal certificate is issued free of charge by the FNMT (the Spanish Royal Mint) on its website.
hacienda.start.cert.p2: There are several ways to get it: request it online and prove your identity in person at an office, by video identification, with your electronic ID card or with the FNMT app on your phone.
hacienda.start.cert.p3: Follow the FNMT instructions to the letter. There are usually four steps: initial setup, request, proving your identity and downloading the certificate.
hacienda.start.cert.c3: I have downloaded and installed it.
hacienda.start.cert.c4: I have made a password-protected backup of the certificate.
hacienda.start.cert.tip: Keep the backup somewhere safe: if you change computer, you import it instead of requesting it again.
hacienda.start.cert.warn: The certificate expires. Put the date in your calendar to renew it before it does.
hacienda.start.reference.title: For the Renta: the reference number
hacienda.start.reference.p1: In the Renta section of the tax website, click «Obtén tu número de referencia» (get your reference number). It asks for your NIF, the expiry date of your ID card and the amount in box 505 of last year’s Renta.
hacienda.start.reference.p2: If you did not file last year, or that box was 0, it asks instead for the last digits of a bank account in your name.
hacienda.start.reference.p3: Keep the number: you will use it during the campaign. If you request a new one, the old one stops working.
hacienda.start.reference.c1: I have box 505 of last year’s Renta at hand.
hacienda.start.reference.c2: I have got my reference number.
hacienda.start.proxy.title: If an accountant files for you: the power of attorney
hacienda.start.proxy.p1: If an accountant or a relative files your taxes, do not give them your passwords: grant them a power of attorney (apoderamiento) in the Agencia Tributaria register.
hacienda.start.proxy.p2: You can grant it online (with Cl@ve, a certificate or the electronic ID card), in person at an Agencia Tributaria office, or with a notarised document.
hacienda.start.proxy.p3: It can be general, for the procedures allowed, or only for specific ones such as the Renta or form 303. If you grant it online, the other person has to accept it before it works.
hacienda.start.proxy.p4: Many accountancy firms are «colaboradores sociales» of the Agencia Tributaria and can file with your written authorisation, without a power of attorney. Ask your accountant what they need.
hacienda.start.proxy.c1: I have talked to my accountant about how they will file.
hacienda.start.proxy.c2: I have granted the power of attorney (if needed) and it is accepted.
hacienda.start.proxy.tip: You can check and revoke your powers of attorney at any time on the tax website.
hacienda.start.deadline1: Do it early: the Cl@ve invitation letter comes by post and takes a few days.
hacienda.start.deadline2: The reference number can be requested before the Renta starts (in the last campaign, from 11 March {filed}).

hacienda.renta.description: How to open Renta WEB, review the draft, file it, pay or get a refund, keep the receipt and fix mistakes.
hacienda.renta.intro: Renta WEB is the Agencia Tributaria tool to review your draft, add what is missing and file your income tax return. It runs in the browser on your computer or phone, nothing to install. If you already have a way to identify yourself (see «Before you start»), it will not take long.
hacienda.renta.prepare.title: Gather your papers
hacienda.renta.prepare.p1: Have at hand your ID, your IBAN, the family changes of the year (wedding, children, moving), the cadastral references of your properties (they are on the IBI property tax bill) and the receipts of anything you can deduct: rent, mortgage, pension plan, donations, union fees…
hacienda.renta.prepare.p2: If you want to know beforehand whether you will pay or get money back, try our Renta calculator.
hacienda.renta.prepare.c1: I have my ID and IBAN at hand.
hacienda.renta.prepare.c2: I have the cadastral references of my properties.
hacienda.renta.prepare.c3: I have the receipts of my deductions.
hacienda.renta.access.title: Open Renta WEB
hacienda.renta.access.p1: Go to sede.agenciatributaria.gob.es, open the Renta section and click the service to process the draft or the return (the one that mentions Renta WEB).
hacienda.renta.access.p2: Identify yourself with Cl@ve, a certificate, the electronic ID card or the reference number. You can also do everything from the official Agencia Tributaria app.
hacienda.renta.access.p3: First it asks you to confirm your tax address (where you live now). If you had already started another day, you can continue with what you saved or start a new return with up-to-date tax data.
hacienda.renta.access.c2: I have confirmed my tax address.
hacienda.renta.access.tip: If it offers you Renta Directa, that is the fast lane for simple returns that need no changes. If you need to change anything, use Renta WEB.
hacienda.renta.personal.title: Check your personal and family details
hacienda.renta.personal.p1: Check your marital status, children, older relatives living with you, disability and region of residence. If anything changed during the year, fix it.
hacienda.renta.personal.p2: If you want to see the joint return, your spouse’s data load when they identify themselves with their reference number or Cl@ve.
hacienda.renta.personal.c1: My personal and family details are right.
hacienda.renta.personal.warn: Your region matters a lot: it decides which regional deductions you can claim.
hacienda.renta.income.title: Check your work income and anything else you received
hacienda.renta.income.p1: Under work income, compare what you see with your employer’s withholding certificate: income, tax withheld and social security contributions. If you had more than one payer (for example unemployment benefit), check they all appear.
hacienda.renta.income.p2: Also look at bank interest, dividends, sales of shares or funds and any grants or benefits you received.
hacienda.renta.income.p3: If you have the PDF of the draft or of your tax data, our draft reader explains it box by box.
hacienda.renta.income.c1: My work income matches my certificate.
hacienda.renta.income.c2: I have checked interest, sales and grants.
hacienda.renta.property.title: Check your properties
hacienda.renta.property.p1: Every home, garage or plot you own must appear with its cadastral reference and your ownership share. Mark your main home correctly.
hacienda.renta.property.p2: A home that is not your main home and is not rented out (for example a holiday home) is taxed as «imputed income» even if you earn nothing from it. If you rent out a home, declare the rent: you can subtract its costs, such as IBI, community fees, insurance or repairs.
hacienda.renta.property.c1: All my properties appear with their cadastral reference.
hacienda.renta.property.c2: I have declared any rents correctly.
hacienda.renta.deductions.title: Look for missing deductions
hacienda.renta.deductions.p1: This is where most money is lost: the tax office does not always know your deductions, especially the regional ones (rent for young people, birth of children, school costs, donations… depending on your region). This year Renta WEB warns about some, but not all.
hacienda.renta.deductions.p2: Check the national ones too: pension plan, union fees, donations, maternity, large family and the main home deduction (only for purchases before 2013).
hacienda.renta.deductions.p3: Our Renta calculator has the deductions of every region so you can see which ones fit you.
hacienda.renta.deductions.c1: I have checked the regional deductions of my region.
hacienda.renta.deductions.c2: I have added the missing deductions.
hacienda.renta.deductions.warn: Only claim deductions you can prove with paperwork: the tax office can ask for it for years.
hacienda.renta.modify.title: How to change something
hacienda.renta.modify.p1: The «Apartados declaración» (return sections) button takes you to any section to change or add data. Many fields open a window that asks for the data one by one.
hacienda.renta.modify.p2: When you finish, use the validate option so the tool warns you about errors. «Vista previa» (preview) shows a PDF of the return, but that PDF cannot be used to file it.
hacienda.renta.modify.p3: You can save and leave: your work is kept so you can continue another day.
hacienda.renta.modify.p4: If you are married, or a single parent with children, compare the individual and the joint return: Renta WEB shows the result of each one in columns.
hacienda.renta.modify.c1: I have compared individual and joint, if it applies.
hacienda.renta.modify.c2: I have validated the return with no errors.
hacienda.renta.submit.title: File the return
hacienda.renta.submit.p1: When you agree with the result, click «Presentar declaración» (file return). If there are several options (individual or joint), choose the one you file.
hacienda.renta.submit.p2: Choose how you pay or get paid (next step), read any warnings, tick «Conforme» (I agree) and click «Firmar y enviar» (sign and send).
hacienda.renta.submit.warn: Check the IBAN before signing: last year’s account may appear.
hacienda.renta.pay.title: If you get a refund or have to pay
hacienda.renta.pay.p1: Refund: enter your IBAN and the tax office pays the money into it. You can follow your refund on the tax website or in the app.
hacienda.renta.pay.p2: To pay, you can set up a direct debit from your account (filing before the direct debit deadline), pay at once with the NRC code your bank gives you, by card or with Bizum, or file with «Reconocimiento de deuda» (acknowledgement of debt) and ask to defer the payment.
hacienda.renta.pay.p3: You can also split the payment in two instalments with no interest: 60 % when you file and 40 % in November.
hacienda.renta.pay.c1: I have chosen how I pay or which account gets the refund.
hacienda.renta.receipt.title: Keep the receipt
hacienda.renta.receipt.p1: At the end you see a confirmation message and a PDF with the date and time of filing and the secure verification code (CSV). Download it and keep it.
hacienda.renta.receipt.p2: If you lose it, you can download it again from the list of filed returns on the tax website.
hacienda.renta.receipt.c1: I have downloaded and kept the receipt.
hacienda.renta.receipt.tip: Keep it with the receipts of your deductions for at least four years: that is how long the tax office has to review it.
hacienda.renta.fix.title: If you made a mistake
hacienda.renta.fix.p1: Open Renta WEB again, click «Modificar declaración presentada» (change filed return), fix it and file a corrective return (box 103). It works whether the mistake is against you or in your favour.
hacienda.renta.fix.p2: If the mistake meant you paid too little and you fix it after the deadline, you pay a surcharge (from 1 %, plus 1 % for each full month late) but no penalty. If it is in your favour, the tax office refunds the difference.
hacienda.renta.fix.p3: You have four years from the end of the filing period to correct it.
hacienda.renta.fix.c1: I have checked whether I need to correct anything.
hacienda.renta.deadline1: Dates of the last campaign (Renta {year} campaign, filed in {filed}): from 8 April to 30 June {filed}.
hacienda.renta.deadline2: If you have to pay by direct debit: file by 25 June {filed} (the charge is made on 30 June).
hacienda.renta.deadline3: If you split the payment: the second instalment (40 %) is paid on 5 November {filed}.
hacienda.renta.deadline4: Help by phone (the «Le Llamamos» plan) from 6 May and at offices from 1 June {filed}, always with an appointment.
hacienda.renta.deadline5: The next campaign usually starts in early April. The tax agency publishes the exact dates beforehand on its website: check them there.
hacienda.m303.title: Form 303 (quarterly VAT) step by step on the tax website
hacienda.m303.description: How to file VAT form 303 on the Tax Agency website: Pre303 or a file, each box, how to pay, deadlines and surcharges.
hacienda.m303.intro: Form 303 is the VAT return you file every quarter: the VAT you charged on your invoices minus the VAT you paid on your expenses. A very common misunderstanding: form 303 is not a file you «attach». It is filled in online, in the form on the tax website, or imported as a file produced by your accounting software.
hacienda.m303.numbers.title: Get your numbers ready
hacienda.m303.numbers.p1: For the quarter you need: the base and VAT of the invoices you issued, split by rate (21 %, 10 %, 4 %), and the base and VAT of the invoices for your business expenses.
hacienda.m303.numbers.p2: Our self-employed draft works out the boxes of forms 303 and 130 from the income and expenses you enter. Prepare it there and keep it open while you fill in the form.
hacienda.m303.numbers.c1: I have the invoices I issued this quarter.
hacienda.m303.numbers.c2: I have the expense invoices with their VAT.
hacienda.m303.numbers.c3: I have prepared the draft in Finanverso.
hacienda.m303.access.title: Open the form
hacienda.m303.access.p1: On the tax website go to Todas las gestiones › Impuestos, tasas y prestaciones patrimoniales › IVA › Modelo 303, and choose filing with the Pre303 help service for the right year.
hacienda.m303.access.p2: Identify yourself with Cl@ve, a certificate or the electronic ID card. Enter your NIF and name, choose the year and the period (1T, 2T, 3T or 4T) and confirm.
hacienda.m303.access.p3: It shows your VAT registration details: check them and carry on with form 303.
hacienda.m303.access.c1: I have opened the form for the right period.
hacienda.m303.access.tip: Pre303 is the official form with help: it fills in some boxes and, if you keep your VAT books on the tax website, it can bring the amounts from there. Always check what it suggests: the figures are your responsibility.
hacienda.m303.file.title: Form or file?
hacienda.m303.file.p1: If you do it by hand, start a new return and fill in the boxes on screen.
hacienda.m303.file.p2: If your accounting software or your accountant gives you a form 303 file in the official format, use «Importar» (import): the form is filled in from that file and you check it before filing.
hacienda.m303.file.p3: You do not attach invoices or PDFs: nothing else is asked for when filing. Keep your invoices in case the tax office asks for them later.
hacienda.m303.file.c1: I know whether I will fill it in by hand or import a file.
hacienda.m303.boxes.title: What goes in each box (the typical self-employed case)
hacienda.m303.boxes.p1: VAT charged: boxes 07, 08 and 09 hold what you invoiced at 21 % (base, rate and VAT); boxes 04, 05 and 06, at 10 %; and boxes 01, 02 and 03, at 4 %. Box 27 is the total VAT charged.
hacienda.m303.boxes.p2: Deductible VAT (what you paid): boxes 28 and 29 hold the base and VAT of your current expenses; boxes 30 and 31, those of capital goods. Box 45 is the total to deduct.
hacienda.m303.boxes.p3: Result: box 46 is the difference (27 − 45). If you have amounts to offset from earlier quarters, they go in boxes 110 and 78. The final result is in box 71.
hacienda.m303.boxes.p4: If you sell to customers in other countries, those operations go in other boxes (for example 59, 60 or 120). If that is your case, read the official instructions or ask your accountant.
hacienda.m303.boxes.p5: The Finanverso self-employed draft shows you these same boxes with their amounts.
hacienda.m303.boxes.c1: I have filled in the VAT charged.
hacienda.m303.boxes.c2: I have filled in the deductible VAT.
hacienda.m303.boxes.warn: You can only deduct the VAT of business expenses with an invoice in your name, with your NIF and the VAT shown separately.
hacienda.m303.check.title: Validate and review
hacienda.m303.check.p1: Click «Validar declaración» (validate). Errors must be fixed; warnings do not stop you filing, but read them.
hacienda.m303.check.p2: «Vista previa» gives you a draft PDF (not valid for filing). «Guardar» saves the return on the tax website to finish later. «Exportar» downloads a file you can import again.
hacienda.m303.check.c1: I have validated with no errors.
hacienda.m303.pay.title: File and pay
hacienda.m303.pay.p1: Click «Presentar declaración» (file). If there is something to pay, choose how:
hacienda.m303.pay.p2: Direct debit: you enter your IBAN and the charge is made at the end of the period. You can only do it if you file before the direct debit deadline, which is shorter (up to the 15th in April, July and October).
hacienda.m303.pay.p3: Pay with an NRC: pay at your bank or from the form itself with «Realizar pago (NRC)» (account charge, card or Bizum) and you get a 22-character NRC code that goes into the return.
hacienda.m303.pay.p4: Acknowledgement of debt (reconocimiento de deuda): you file without paying and then ask to defer or offset it from «Tramitar deuda» on the receipt. It is also how you pay by transfer from a bank that is not a collaborating bank.
hacienda.m303.pay.p5: If the result is negative you pay nothing and offset it in the next quarters. A refund can only be requested in the 4th quarter, unless you are in the monthly refund register.
hacienda.m303.pay.p6: To finish, click «Firmar y enviar» (sign and send), review the summary, tick your agreement and confirm.
hacienda.m303.pay.c1: I have chosen how to pay.
hacienda.m303.pay.c2: I have signed and sent the return.
hacienda.m303.receipt.title: Keep the receipt
hacienda.m303.receipt.p1: You get a PDF with the receipt number, date and time, the secure verification code (CSV) and a copy of the return. Download it.
hacienda.m303.receipt.p2: Write down the receipt number: if you need to correct form 303 later, you will be asked for it.
hacienda.m303.receipt.c1: I have kept the receipt PDF.
hacienda.m303.fix.title: If you made a mistake or are late
hacienda.m303.fix.p1: To correct a form 303 already filed, you file a corrective return (autoliquidación rectificativa) for the same period, ticking that box and entering the receipt number of the original.
hacienda.m303.fix.p2: If you file late without the tax office asking you to, there is no penalty but there is a surcharge: 1 % plus another 1 % for each full month late and, after 12 months, 15 % plus late-payment interest. The surcharge is reduced by 25 % if you pay on time, in the cases the law allows.
hacienda.m303.fix.p3: Even if you invoiced nothing in a quarter, form 303 is still filed (there is a «sin actividad», no activity, option), except in special cases.
hacienda.m303.fix.c1: If I was late, I have filed as soon as possible.
hacienda.m303.deadline4: 4th quarter: 1 to 30 January of the following year.
hacienda.m303.deadline5: With direct debit: up to 15 April, July and October; in January, a few days before the 30th (in 2026, up to 27 January).
hacienda.m303.deadline6: If the last day is a Saturday, Sunday or public holiday, the deadline moves to the next working day.
hacienda.m130.title: Form 130 (income tax instalment) step by step
hacienda.m130.description: Who has to file form 130, the 70 % withholding exemption, the boxes of section I, the box 13 reduction, how to file and pay it, and its deadlines.
hacienda.m130.intro: With form 130 you pay in advance, every quarter, 20 % of what you earn as a self-employed person, on account of your Renta. Like form 303, nothing is attached: it is filled in online on the tax website or imported as a file from your accounting software.
hacienda.m130.who.title: Do you have to file it?
hacienda.m130.who.p1: It is filed by self-employed people under direct assessment (normal or simplified). If you are under modules (objective assessment), yours is form 131.
hacienda.m130.who.p2: If you are a professional, you do not have to file it when, the year before, at least 70 % of your business income had tax withheld (for example because you mainly invoice companies that withhold income tax). If you are just starting, that 70 % is checked on the quarter itself.
hacienda.m130.who.p3: If in doubt, check last year’s invoices or ask your accountant.
hacienda.m130.who.c1: I have checked whether I have to file form 130.
hacienda.m130.numbers.title: Work out the cumulative figures
hacienda.m130.numbers.p1: The key point: form 130 is cumulative from 1 January. In the 2nd quarter you enter the income and expenses from January to June, not just April to June.
hacienda.m130.numbers.p2: Our self-employed draft works out every box of form 130 for you.
hacienda.m130.numbers.c1: I have the cumulative income of the year.
hacienda.m130.numbers.c2: I have the cumulative deductible expenses.
hacienda.m130.numbers.c3: I have what I paid in earlier forms 130 and my withholdings.
hacienda.m130.access.title: Open the form
hacienda.m130.access.p1: On the tax website go to Todas las gestiones › Impuestos, tasas y prestaciones patrimoniales › Impuesto sobre la Renta de las Personas Físicas › Modelo 130, and choose filing for the right year.
hacienda.m130.access.p2: Identify yourself with Cl@ve, a certificate or the electronic ID card, enter your details and choose the period.
hacienda.m130.access.p3: You can start a new return, load a saved one or import a file from your accounting software. If you keep record books, you can import them too so the data are filled in.
hacienda.m130.access.c1: I have opened the form for the right period.
hacienda.m130.boxes.title: Section I: the boxes
hacienda.m130.boxes.p1: Box 01: cumulative income of the year. Box 02: cumulative deductible expenses, including depreciation. Box 03: the difference (01 − 02), your net income.
hacienda.m130.boxes.p2: Box 04: 20 % of box 03, if positive (otherwise zero). Box 05: what you already paid in earlier forms 130 this year. Box 06: the tax withheld on your invoices, also cumulative. Box 07: 04 − 05 − 06.
hacienda.m130.boxes.p3: Section II is for farming, livestock, forestry and fishing: if that is not you, leave it blank.
hacienda.m130.boxes.c1: I have filled in boxes 01 to 07.
hacienda.m130.boxes.tip: In Ceuta and Melilla the box 04 percentage is lower (8 %) for income earned there.
hacienda.m130.reduce.title: The reduction (box 13) and the result
hacienda.m130.reduce.p1: Box 12: the sum of boxes 07 and 11, never below zero.
hacienda.m130.reduce.p2: Box 13: if last year your net business income was 12,000 € or less, you subtract an amount every quarter: 100 € up to 9,000 €; 75 € from 9,000.01 to 10,000 €; 50 € from 10,000.01 to 11,000 €; and 25 € from 11,000.01 to 12,000 €. If you had no business last year, it counts as zero.
hacienda.m130.reduce.p3: Box 14: 12 − 13. Box 15: negative results of earlier quarters this year not yet subtracted. Box 16: main home loan deduction, only in specific cases (home bought before 2013, among other requirements). Box 17: 14 − 15 − 16. Box 19: the final result.
hacienda.m130.reduce.p4: If box 19 is negative in the 1st, 2nd or 3rd quarter, you mark it «a deducir» (to deduct) and subtract it in the next ones. In the 4th quarter, or if it is zero, the return is «negativa»: you pay nothing but get nothing back; that is settled in the Renta.
hacienda.m130.reduce.c1: I have checked whether the box 13 reduction applies to me.
hacienda.m130.pay.title: Validate, file and pay
hacienda.m130.pay.p1: Click «Validar declaración» (validate) and fix the errors. Then follow the filing buttons of the form.
hacienda.m130.pay.p2: If there is something to pay, the ways are the same as for form 303: direct debit with your IBAN, payment with an NRC (bank, card or Bizum with «Realizar pago (NRC)») or acknowledgement of debt to ask to defer it.
hacienda.m130.pay.p3: Click «Firmar y enviar» (sign and send), review the summary, tick your agreement and confirm.
hacienda.m130.pay.c1: I have filed and paid (or set up the direct debit).
hacienda.m130.receipt.title: Receipt and corrections
hacienda.m130.receipt.p1: Download the receipt PDF: receipt number, date and time, secure verification code (CSV) and a copy of the return.
hacienda.m130.receipt.p2: If you made a mistake and paid too little, file a supplementary return (complementaria), ticking that box and entering the receipt number of the previous one. If you paid too much, you ask for a correction (rectificación).
hacienda.m130.receipt.p3: If you file late, the surcharges are the same as for form 303: 1 % plus 1 % for each full month and, after 12 months, 15 % plus interest.
hacienda.m130.deadline4: 4th quarter: 1 to 30 January of the following year.
hacienda.m130.deadline5: With direct debit the filing deadline is shorter: check it in the taxpayer calendar.
hacienda.m130.deadline6: It is filed on the same dates as form 303, and if the last day is not a working day it moves to the next one.

tools.renta.guide.why.ccaa: Each region has its own scale for half of the tax and its own deductions: it changes what you pay and what you can deduct.
tools.renta.guide.why.age: From 65 the personal minimum rises by 1,150 €, and from 75 by 1,400 € more: you pay less tax.
tools.renta.guide.why.income: Pensions and unemployment benefits do not give the deduction of up to 340 € for work income, and only active workers add the extra expenses for disability.
tools.renta.guide.why.disability: With 33 % or more the minimum rises by 3,000 € (12,000 € from 65 %, with the assistance expenses) and, if you work, so do the deductible work expenses.
tools.renta.guide.why.active: Only active workers with a disability add 3,500 € of expenses (7,750 € from 65 % or with reduced mobility).
tools.renta.guide.why.family: Each child under 25 and each ascendant over 65 living with you raise the family minimum and open deductions such as maternity or large family.
tools.renta.guide.why.joint: As a married couple, or with your minor children if you have no spouse, you can file a single return. We work out both options and tell you which is better.
tools.renta.guide.why.property: Rent you charge is taxed, and empty properties or second homes add an imputed income (1.1 % or 2 % of the cadastral value).
tools.renta.guide.why.savings: Interest, dividends and gains go to the savings base, with its own scale (from 19 % to 30 %).
tools.renta.guide.why.plan: What you pay into a pension plan lowers the base: up to 1,500 € (more with employer contributions) and 30 % of your net work income.
tools.renta.guide.why.housing: Many regions deduct part of the rent of your home, and mortgages on homes bought before 2013 keep the State deduction of the transitional regime.

tools.renta.joint.singleHint: If you live with the other parent you can file jointly with your children, but without the 2,150 € reduction. With shared custody, you both have to agree on who files it.

tools.renta.joint.note.couple: The joint return has a single taxpayer minimum (5,550 €) with the age and disability of each spouse, the joint taxation reduction ({amount} applied, 3,400 € at most) and the joint income limits of the deductions (arts. 84 and 82 of the IRPF Act).
tools.renta.joint.note.single: The single-parent joint return lowers the base by {amount} (2,150 € at most; nothing if you live with the other parent).
tools.renta.joint.note.childrenToOne: If all the children went to {who}, the individual returns would add up to {amount}. That is only possible when the other parent has no right to the minimum (for instance, does not live with them): if you live together the minimum is split in equal parts (art. 61.1 of the IRPF Act) and the table applies.
tools.renta.joint.note.oneGeneral: We counted 2,000 € of "other expenses" for each of you who earns from work. The Tax Agency manual says these expenses apply "per family unit" without making this amount clear: if only one counted, the joint return would be {amount} worse.
tools.renta.joint.note.lowPay: The individual returns apply the deduction for work income (up to 340 € each): {amount}. The Tax Agency does not make clear how it works in a joint return when you both earn or have other income, so we left it out: the joint return could be up to {amount} better.
tools.renta.joint.note.assumptions: Assumptions: the children have no income; the deductions marked, the properties, the rents and your dependants go in your return; in the individual returns the children's minimum is split in equal parts.
tools.renta.joint.warning: This is an estimate. Joint or individual is chosen every year and, once the return is filed, it can only be changed by filing new returns within the voluntary filing period; after it, it cannot be changed. Check it first with the Tax Agency draft, which works out both options.

app.autonomo.vatr.warn.offsetNotApplied: This quarter you do not apply the VAT to offset although you could: it stays for the next ones (box 87).
app.autonomo.vatr.warn.simplified: You are in módulos: the simplified regime part of the 303 is not worked out here.
app.autonomo.vatr.warn.reagp: The REAGP sales are not in the 303: you collect the compensation from the buyer.
app.autonomo.vatr.warn.reverseIssued: Invoices with reverse charge: they must say «inversión del sujeto pasivo» and carry no VAT.

app.autonomo.activity.title: The activity of the year: depreciation, grants and regime
app.autonomo.activity.hint: What the invoices of the quarter do not say: the assets you depreciate, the grants and the annual figures the Renta needs. A guide: check it against your draft.
app.autonomo.activity.regimeHint.simplif: The one of most of the self-employed (up to 600,000 € of turnover). Simplified depreciation table and 5 % of hard-to-justify expenses (up to 2,000 €).
app.autonomo.activity.regimeHint.normal: Over 600,000 € of turnover or by choice. Official table of the corporate tax, deductible provisions and no 5 % of hard-to-justify expenses.
app.autonomo.activity.regimeHint.objecti: In modules you file the 131, not the 130. The app works out the annual yield of farming; not that of other activities.
app.autonomo.activity.agrarian: Farming, livestock, forestry or fishing activity
app.autonomo.activity.agrarianHint: The 130 is filled in its section II: 2 % of the income of each quarter (with the current grants, without the capital ones) less the withholdings of the quarter.
app.autonomo.activity.assetsHint: Computer, furniture, vehicle, premises… The cost is what you paid without the VAT you deduct. It is depreciated by whole months from when you start using it. A car only counts if used only for the activity; a building, the part you use. With its VAT, those of earlier years go to the regularisation of investment goods of the 303.
app.autonomo.activity.assetsHintModules: Depreciation table of modules (groups 1 to 10). Forestry deducts no depreciation.
app.autonomo.activity.subsidiesHint: Current (including the CAP ones): income of the year. Capital: as the asset they pay for is depreciated. First installation of young farmers: a quarter each of four years. Aid for giving up, uprooting or disasters of the 5th additional provision is not taxed. A grant tied to the price of what you sell goes with the income of the quarter, with its VAT.
app.autonomo.activity.provisionsHint: Normal modality only (for example, customers who do not pay). Taken off in the fourth quarter.
app.autonomo.activity.retaFixHint: What you paid (+) or got back (−) this year when your fees were regularised. It goes to the Renta, not to the 130.
app.autonomo.activity.selfConsumption: Self-consumption (what you keep from your activity, at market price)
app.autonomo.activity.stockChangeHint: Closing stock less opening stock: positive when it grows, negative when it falls. For the Renta only.
app.autonomo.activity.compensations: Compensations of the special agricultural regime (REAGP)
app.autonomo.activity.compensationsHint: The 12 % (farming or forestry) or 10.5 % (livestock or fishing) your buyers pay you (art. 130 of the VAT Act). It is income of your activity; in the REAGP you file no 303 for it.
app.autonomo.activity.paid130Hint: Box 19 of each 130 filed. Left empty, the app uses its own estimate (and says so).
app.autonomo.activity.asset.name: Asset
app.autonomo.activity.asset.accumulated: Depreciated up to 31-12 of last year (empty: worked out)
app.autonomo.activity.method.free300: Free depreciation (new, up to 300 €; 601.01 € in modules)
app.autonomo.activity.subsidy.name: Grant
app.autonomo.activity.subsidy.noAsset: None (land or another that is not depreciated)
app.autonomo.activity.modules.rowsHint: Income of the year from each product, with its grants and compensations (order of modules of the year, anexo I). If a reduction order lowers the index in your municipality, type it.
app.autonomo.activity.modules.staffShare: Cost of salaried staff (% of income)
app.autonomo.activity.modules.rentedShar: % of the yield on rented land
app.autonomo.activity.modules.irrigatedS: % of the yield on land irrigated with electricity
app.autonomo.activity.modules.externalMe: Only means of production of others (0.75)
app.autonomo.activity.modules.boughtFeed: More than half of the feed bought (0.50)
app.autonomo.activity.modules.forestPlan: Forestry with an approved plan of 20 years or more (0.80)
app.autonomo.activity.modules.youngFarme: Young farmer in the first 5 years (25 % reduction)
app.autonomo.activity.notCalculated: not worked out: copy it from your draft

app.autonomo.activity.warning.priorTotal: The earlier quarters come from the totals of your last 130: check that the whole year is in the app.
app.autonomo.activity.warning.objective: An activity in modules outside farming: the app does not work out its yield.
app.autonomo.activity.warning.payments13: Some payments of the 130 are the app's estimate: type what you really paid.

app.autonomo.activity.warning.investment: Some expenses are marked as investment goods but there are no assets: add them so their depreciation counts.
app.autonomo.activity.warning.capitalNoA: A capital grant does not finance a depreciated asset: it is taxed when you sell it, not worked out here.
app.autonomo.activity.warning.exemptAid: There is exempt aid (5th additional provision): it is not added.
app.autonomo.activity.warning.provisions: In the simplified modality provisions are not deducted: they are in the 5 % of hard-to-justify expenses.
app.autonomo.activity.warning.assetNotes: Some assets are not depreciated as typed (coefficient outside the table, partial use, limit of free depreciation…): check them.

app.autonomo.activity.warning.modules: Check the modules: a year without a known order, a product without a processed index or over 250,000 € of income (out of modules).

wizard.renta.step.result: Your result and how to file it
wizard.renta.hint.ccaa: Where your home was on 31 December. For example: “Andalucía” or “Comunidad de Madrid”.
wizard.renta.hint.age: Type the number only. For example: 67.
wizard.renta.hint.income: Pick the closest one. Then we ask for the amounts of the year: they are on the certificate from your employer or from Social Security.
wizard.renta.hint.disability: Only with an official disability certificate. Otherwise choose “No”.
wizard.renta.hint.family: Children under 25 living with you, or parents or grandparents over 65 living with you.
wizard.renta.hint.joint: A joint return is one return for the whole family. We tell you whether it pays off.
wizard.renta.hint.housing: The home you live in. For example: you pay €600 rent a month.
wizard.renta.hint.property: For example: a flat you rent out, or a house in the village you do not rent.
wizard.renta.hint.savings: For example: interest on an account, dividends from shares, or selling a fund or crypto.
wizard.renta.hint.plan: What you paid into a pension plan in the year (yours or your employer's).
wizard.renta.hint.payers: A payer is whoever paid you: your employer, unemployment benefit (SEPE) or Social Security. For example: you worked for two companies.
wizard.renta.hint.activity: For example: you issue invoices as self-employed or you run a shop.
wizard.renta.hint.donations: For example: you give €10 a month to a charity or a foundation.
wizard.renta.hint.others: There are deductions for nursery, large families, electric cars, rent for young people… Look only if you want: in the next step we ask you about the ones that fit you best.
wizard.renta.hint.draft: An optional shortcut. If you have it, we read it on your device (it is not sent anywhere) and fill in many answers for you.
wizard.renta.hint.review: We show you, one by one, the deductions that could fit you. Answer “Yes”, “No” or “Later”.
wizard.renta.hint.result: With what you answered, this is what you would get. If you don't see it yet, press the button to work it out.
wizard.renta.hint.boxes: Each box number is a square of the official form. Copy them and compare them with your draft.
wizard.renta.hint.file: Finanverso does not file anything for you: you do it on the Tax Agency's website. This is how:
wizard.renta.help.payers: If you had more than one payer and what the second and later ones paid is over €1,500 a year, you may have to file even if you earn under €22,000.
wizard.renta.help.activity: The income and expenses of your self-employed activity go into the return. If you keep your invoices in Finanverso, in Self-employed press “Prepare my income tax return” and they will come here.
wizard.renta.help.donations: You get back 80 % of the first €250 donated and 40 % of the rest, if the body is under Law 49/2002 and you have the donation certificate.
wizard.renta.help.others: A deduction is an amount taken off what you pay. Some are the State's and others your region's.
wizard.renta.help.draft: The draft is the return the Tax Agency prepares with the data it has about you. You download it as a PDF from Renta WEB.
wizard.renta.help.review: A deduction is money taken off your tax. “Later” puts it aside for you to look at calmly.
wizard.renta.help.result: It is an estimate with what you answered. Renta WEB gives the real result when you file.
wizard.renta.help.boxes: A box is a numbered square of form 100 (the income tax return). The base is the amount the tax is worked out on.
wizard.renta.q.payers: Did you have more than one payer this year?
wizard.renta.q.activity: Are you self-employed or do you run a business?

wizard.renta.q.donations: Did you donate to a charity or foundation?

tools.renta.investCard.title: My investments (crypto, funds, shares)
tools.renta.investCard.hint: Files from Binance, Coinbase, Kraken, Degiro, Revolut, funds… or your bank's PDF. We work out the gain or loss of each sale.
tools.renta.investCard.link: Have you invested in crypto, funds or shares?
wizard.renta.help.investImport: A capital gain is what you make (or lose) when you sell something for more (or less) than it cost you. It goes into the savings base. If you sold crypto, funds or shares, you must declare it even at a loss.

wizard.autonomo.intro: We walk you through it: first your activity, then your invoices, and at the end the forms ready to copy. Stop whenever you like: it saves by itself.
wizard.autonomo.q.period: Which quarter do you want to prepare?
wizard.autonomo.hint.period: A quarter is three months. For example: January to March is Q1, filed from 1 to 20 April.
wizard.autonomo.help.period: Each quarter you file form 303 (VAT) and, if it applies, form 130 (income tax in advance). We prepare them here for you to copy.
wizard.autonomo.hint.regime: If you don't know, almost every self-employed person is in the general regime.
wizard.autonomo.help.regime: VAT is the tax you add to your invoices and then pay to the Tax Agency, minus the VAT of your expenses. The regime is the way it is worked out.
wizard.autonomo.opt.regime.general: General regime (the usual: I add VAT to my invoices)
wizard.autonomo.q.retained: Is income tax withheld from at least 70 % of what you invoice?
wizard.autonomo.hint.retained: It happens if you work mostly for companies and take 15 % (or 7 %) off your invoices.
wizard.autonomo.help.retained: The withholding is the part of your invoice your client pays to the Tax Agency for you. If at least 70 % of last year's income had it, you don't file form 130.
wizard.autonomo.opt.retained.yes: Yes, almost everything I invoice has it
wizard.autonomo.opt.retained.no: No, or I sell mostly to individuals
wizard.autonomo.q.simplified: Is your bookkeeping in the simplified direct estimation?
wizard.autonomo.hint.simplified: It's the most common: if your business invoices under €600,000 a year and you didn't choose otherwise, it's you.
wizard.autonomo.help.simplified: It lets you take off 5 % more of “hard-to-justify” expenses (up to €2,000 a year) without proving them.
wizard.autonomo.opt.simplified.no: No, I'm in the normal direct estimation
wizard.autonomo.q.home: Do you work from home, use a vehicle only for work or pay for health insurance?
wizard.autonomo.hint.home: For example: you use a room at home as an office. Part of those costs can be deducted.
wizard.autonomo.help.home: A deductible expense is what you pay to work and can take off your income to pay less.
wizard.autonomo.q.files: How do you want to bring your invoices?
wizard.autonomo.hint.files: You can upload the spreadsheet of your invoicing software, your invoice PDFs or your bank statement. They are read on your device.
wizard.autonomo.help.files: Issued invoices are the ones you make to your clients; received ones, those of your expenses (power, adviser, supplies…).
wizard.autonomo.opt.files.manual: I type the totals by hand
wizard.autonomo.manualLater: Fine: in step 4 you will type the income and expenses of the quarter.
wizard.autonomo.missing.files: Upload at least one file, or choose “I type the totals by hand”.
wizard.autonomo.imported: You have {count} invoices imported. Add more or go on.
wizard.autonomo.q.prior: Have you already filed form 130 for the earlier quarters?
wizard.autonomo.hint.prior: If you filed it with another tool or an adviser, type its totals and we won't repeat the sum.
wizard.autonomo.help.prior: Form 130 adds up: each quarter is worked out with the whole year so far, minus what you already paid.
wizard.autonomo.hint.invoices: Look at the invoices marked in yellow and the warnings: fix what needs it. The rest is fine.
wizard.autonomo.help.invoices: Sometimes a PDF doesn't say the VAT rate or the date. We show you those invoices here to complete them.
wizard.autonomo.hint.noInvoices: You haven't imported invoices: nothing to check. Go on to the next step.
wizard.autonomo.q.amounts: Your income and expenses of quarter {n}
wizard.autonomo.hint.amounts: If you imported invoices, they are already added up. If not, type the totals without VAT here.
wizard.autonomo.help.amounts: The base is the amount without VAT. For example: a €121 invoice with 21 % VAT has a €100 base.
wizard.autonomo.advanced: More options (pro rata, VAT to offset, cash accounting…)
wizard.autonomo.hint.prepare: Press the button and we tell you how much to pay, in words and box by box.
wizard.autonomo.help.prepare: A box is a numbered square of the official form. Copy each number into the same square on the Tax Agency's website.
wizard.autonomo.q.withholdings: Do you pay employees, professionals with withholding, or the rent of premises?
wizard.autonomo.hint.withholdings: For example: you have an employee, you pay an adviser or you rent an office.
wizard.autonomo.help.withholdings: If so, each quarter you pay in what you withheld from them: form 111 (employees and professionals) and form 115 (rent).
wizard.autonomo.q.assets: Did you buy something big for work or get grants this year?
wizard.autonomo.hint.assets: For example: a computer, a car or machinery, or a grant.
wizard.autonomo.help.assets: What lasts several years is not deducted at once: it is spread over the years (depreciation). We work it out for you.
wizard.autonomo.hint.warnings: Read the warnings before filing. They don't block: they are things worth a look.
wizard.autonomo.hint.noWarnings: We see nothing odd. Well done!
wizard.autonomo.help.warnings: A warning is something that might be wrong (a repeated invoice, an empty quarter…). You decide whether to fix it.
wizard.autonomo.hint.downloads: The preview of each form (to copy it), the file for the Tax Agency website and the summary of the year.
wizard.autonomo.help.downloads: The file for the website can be imported on the Tax Agency's website instead of copying box by box. Always check it before filing.
wizard.autonomo.noDraft: You haven't worked out the quarter yet (step 4): when you do, its PDF and files will be here.
wizard.autonomo.hint.renta: When the year ends, take your income, expenses, withholdings and form 130 payments to the return with one button.
wizard.autonomo.nothingYet: When you have data of your activity, you can take it to the return here.
wizard.autonomo.finale: Your quarter is ready. Copy it on the Tax Agency's website within the deadline (shown in step 4, next to the result).
wizard.autonomo.notFiled: This is guidance only: Finanverso does not file anything with the Tax Agency. If in doubt, have it checked by a registered tax adviser.
